description:
We are the tech-and-design duo behind Pingvin Studio, combining 25+ years of experience in software development and digital design.

Building on our complementary backgrounds, alongside a passion for STEAM and experience in NASA citizen science through Zooniverse, we aim to turn scientific data into meaningful, accessible, and engaging digital experiences.
summary:
STILL OUT THERE: Stories of Earth's Forgotten Explorers is an interactive 3D web application designed for school-age children (ages 8–12) that brings NASA’s silent robotic scouts and spacecraft on the Moon and Mars back to life through first-person storytelling. While young space enthusiasts often hear only about active missions, legendary pioneers like Apollo 11’s Eagle, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, Surveyor 3, Ingenuity, Opportunity, and InSight remain standing on distant worlds as monuments to human curiosity.
Our application transforms dense archival mission data into an accessible, story-driven museum experience. Children explore interactive 3D globes of the Moon and Mars, listen to narrated first-person stories from illustrated robotic characters, inspect real NASA archival photography, and solve six hands-on STEM mini-challenges. By turning complex engineering and planetary science into an emotional, interactive journey, STILL OUT THERE inspires the next generation of explorers to remember the machines that paved the way.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

STILL OUT THERE is an interactive educational web application built for children ages 8–12 to discover six historic NASA missions resting on the Moon and Mars:

The Moon: Apollo 11 Lunar Module (Eagle), Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV), and Surveyor 3.

Mars: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, Opportunity Rover, and InSight Lander.

Users begin by entering their name and launching into a 3D orbital Mission Hub where they can toggle between the Moon and Mars. Clicking any glowing mission pin introduces a custom illustrated character that tells its true historical story in three short, accessible sentences with built-in voice narration. To ensure young learners engage with the narrative rather than skipping ahead, we implemented a two-step "Story Gate" that unlocks the mission's STEM mini-challenge only after the user reads or listens to all three story segments. Each mission also features a "Did You Know?" science card and an interactive viewer displaying real NASA archival photography from the landing site.

Completing each mission unlocks one of six custom Mission Badges (visual bootprint matching, Lunar Rover materials quiz, Surveyor 3 antenna alignment, Ingenuity rotor RPM math, Opportunity dust-storm solar panel cleanup, and InSight converted seismic marsquake audio sorting). Collecting all 6/6 badges generates a personalized, printable Dual Space Boarding Pass (Sea of Tranquility & Jezero Crater).

Design Process, User Testing & Intended Impact

When designing for ages 8–12, we prioritized narrative empathy, visual clarity, and audio accessibility. During early prototype testing with children in our target age group, we observed that kids intuitively navigated the 3D globes but tended to click straight to mini-games without reading the historical context. Based on this feedback, we added the Story Gate mechanic and first-person voice narration, resulting in higher engagement with both the scientific facts and archival photos. Our goal is to bridge the gap between technical space archives and young imaginations.

Tools, Technologies & Transparency

Web Technologies: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, interactive 3D globe rendering (WebGL), Web Speech API (voice narration), and Web Audio API (synthesized UI sound effects).

Visuals & Content: Custom character illustrations created by our team with AI-assisted illustration tools and post-processed for web, paired with authentic archival imagery from NASA/JPL-Caltech. Super Intelligence (SI) tools were also used to assist with code prototyping and English text refinement, while all scientific facts were verified against official NASA mission records.
